summary: Daniel P. Brown (1948–2022) specialized in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Geshe Wangyal and served as a professor at Harvard Medical School from circa 1982 to 2020.
Daniel R. Tuzzeo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his thesis at Florida State University, where he studied under advisors Jimmy Yu, Bryan J. Cuevas, and Joseph Hellweg.

Daniel Schlumberger (1904–1972) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Strasbourg (circa 1923–1925), succeeded Joseph Hackin, and held a post at Princeton University (circa 1966–1970).

Daniel Sperber (born 1940) works in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Kol Torah, Yeshivah of Flatbush, Kilburn Grammar School, and University College London (circa 1963–1968), he held posts at Bar-Ilan University (circa 1968) and Open University of Israel.

Daniel Stuart Capper is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA and MA at the University of Virginia, studying under Robert P. Scharlemann and Jeffrey Hopkins, and received his PhD from the University of Chicago (attested 2000).

Daniel Timothy Aitken specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at the University of Tasmania, having studied under teachers Parimal G. Patil, Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, and Jay L. Garfield.

Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Virginia. In 2010, he held posts as an instructor at both the University of Virginia and Mary Baldwin University.
Daniela Berti works in Indology and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Siena and was attested as a fellow at Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya in 2004.

Daniela Bevilacqua specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned PhDs from Sapienza University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University, and was a postdoctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London as attested in 2020.
Daniele Cuneo is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held a post at Sorbonne University (attested 2018) and a faculty position at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).
Danielle Feller is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Lausanne in 2001 under doctoral supervisor Johannes Bronkhorst. She also studied under Ganesh Umakant Thite.

Danielle Jacquart (born 1947) is a scholar in history and archaeology. She studied at the École des chartes (circa 1967–1971) and held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études from circa 1990 to 2016.

Danping Long specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology. As attested in 2026, she has studied as a doctoral student at the University of Munich and the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.

Danuta Stasik (born 1956) is an Indologist. She studied at the University of Warsaw (circa 1975–1980) under Maria Krzysztof Byrski (circa 1980–1989), and held posts at the University of Warsaw, including in 1986 and circa 1980.

Dasharatha Sharma (1903–1976) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at the University of Delhi, he held leadership posts at Hindu College, Jai Narain Vyas University, the University of Delhi, and the Rajasthan Oriental Research Institute.

Daud Ali (born 1964) is an Indologist and historian. He studied at the College of William & Mary and the University of Chicago under Ronald Inden. He taught history at SOAS (circa 1995–2005) and joined the University of Pennsylvania in 2009.

Daud Rahbar (1926–2013) studied at Government College University, Lahore, and the University of Cambridge. Specializing in religious studies, he held posts at Punjab, Oriental College, McGill, Ankara, Wisconsin-Madison, and ultimately Boston University (circa 1968–1996).
David A. Dilworth (born 1934) is a scholar of Japanology and philosophy. He studied under Masao Abe and Valdo H. Viglielmo, and he taught Steve Odin.

David A. Hall is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shōshin Ichishima and earned a doctorate from UC Berkeley (1990). He was a visiting scholar at Taisho University (1977) and department chair at Montgomery College (attested 2019).
David Azzopardi is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. As attested in 2010, he completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby.
